category_span.note: The spec requires the 96 to span six axes. This 12-card slice is CONTIGUOUS in the library, so it covers three of them as PRIMARY and one more as secondary. It does not, and cannot, cover all six on its own - research-and-evidence and security-governance-and-risk fall in sibling slices.

distinctness.method: Two mechanical fingerprints, compared across all 66 pairs. (1) Jaccard overlap of the declared mechanism_signature token sets. (2) A structural fingerprint = the stage-kind multiset plus the set of gate expressions.
distinctness.HONEST_LIMIT: The 0.000 overlap is WEAKER evidence than it looks: the mechanism tokens are author-written, so an author who names every mechanism differently gets a low score for free. The load-bearing check is the STRUCTURAL fingerprint, which compares what the workflows do and cannot be satisfied by renaming - the 12 shapes differ genuinely (stage-kind multisets range from {task:6,gate:3} to {task:5,gate:5,subworkflow:2,loop:1,repair_loop:1}).
distinctness.detector_control: test_control_the_distinctness_detector_fires_on_a_planted_duplicate plants a verbatim clone with a new id - the 'renamed copy' the spec forbids - and requires all three checks to trip (signature equality, Jaccard 1.0, fingerprint collision), then requires a genuinely different blueprint NOT to trip them. Without this, 66/66 at 0.000 would be indistinguishable from a no-op comparison.
closest_conceptual_pairs_examined: 74 vs 76 - both concern trustworthy measurement. 74 asks whether the measuring DEVICE is sound (static inspection of a command string, no fixture); 76 assumes a sound device and asks whether the SYSTEM moved (a pinned case set, a variance band, a degraded-config control). Different subject, different stage graph, zero shared tokens.

78 vs 79 - both audit a UI. 78 measures the RUNNING app and can read computed contrast; 79 audits SOURCE and reaches conditionally-rendered surfaces the runtime cannot, with a second fan-out per finding. Kept separate on the card's own grounds.

83 vs 84 - both consolidate documentation. 83 clusters MANY caveats into a new principle and can end in a SCRIPT rather than a document; 84 takes ONE fact and adjudicates which of its statements is authoritative, ending in a pointer rewrite plus a supersession register.

defects_found_and_fixed_while_building: work-unit.schema.json sets minLength 10 on retry_policy, so a bare 'none' fails - and because draft-2020-12 discards annotations from a failed subschema, that ONE short string also cascaded into an unevaluatedProperties error at the STAGE level, which reads as an unknown-property finding. Ten bare 'none' strings produced 22 errors, 12 of them cascades. Fixed at source: bp7_common.work_unit now raises on a retry string under 10 characters, so it cannot recur silently.
The DSL expression grammar has NO arithmetic - 'a + b >= c' fails to parse at the '+'. Two workflow-level stopping rules used it and were rewritten as single-counter comparisons.

DSL-SEM-014 (advisory) revealed a genuine cross-implementation conflict: a COUNCIL stopping rule must parse under both the DSL grammar and councilspec's metric registry, but the DSL tokenizer rejects ':' at offset 6, so councilspec's `custom:<name>` escape hatch is UNUSABLE inside a DSL council stage. Council rule text is therefore restricted to the 51 registry metrics. The registry encoding chosen (minority_report_present == true for 'both verdicts recorded') is documented inline in the blueprint so a reader does not take the metric name literally.

A loop convergence expression referenced target_composite, which was neither a declared metric nor a param (DSL-SEM-008). It is a threshold, so it was declared as a param - the semantically correct fix rather than adding a fake metric.
One of my own checks was case-sensitive on 'Settling experiment' and reported a defect in a correct artifact. The detector was wrong, not the subject; fixed the check.
